documents.body:
Routine 3-month f/u. Energy improving since November. Stools dark on iron, no red blood he's seen. Breathing on exertion unchanged - stops halfway up hills. No chest pain, no fainting. No falls. Bowels ok with daily docusate.

Exam: vitals as charted. Color better than November. Harsh systolic murmur RUSB, mechanical click. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet intact.

A/P:
1. Anemia - CBC today; the acute blood-loss component from November has settled, iron deficiency still being treated. Continue ferrous sulfate.
2. DM2 - A1c. HTN at goal. CKD 3a - BMP.
3. Mechanical MVR - INR, warfarin 5 mg nightly.
RTC 3 months.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 05/18/2026

CC: tired and short of breath x 2 days.

HPI: 75M, mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, recurrent GI bleeding from cecal angiodysplasia (APC 01/2025, observation 11/2025), iron deficiency on oral iron, severe aortic stenosis. Two days of fatigue and breathlessness. On questioning he has had maroon-colored stools on and off for several months, which he put down to his diet and did not mention to anyone. No chest pain. No syncope. No abdominal pain.

Meds: warfarin 5 mg, aspirin 81, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, amlodipine 5, ferrous sulfate 325.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 92, SpO2 96% RA. Pale, comfortable at rest. Harsh, late-peaking systolic murmur at the right second intercostal space radiating to the neck; mechanical click. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, nondistended. Rectal: maroon stool in the vault.

Labs: Hgb 9.8, MCV 89, BUN 28, Cr 1.2, INR 2.9.

MDM: GI bleeding in an anticoagulated patient with a mechanical mitral valve; elevated BUN raises the possibility of an upper source. Hemodynamically stable. GI consulted - admit for upper endoscopy and colonoscopy. Warfarin held; heparin infusion per hospital team once INR below goal. Type and screen sent; no transfusion indicated at this hemoglobin.

Disposition: admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - GI Bleeding
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 05/18/2026  Discharge 05/21/2026

Reason for admission: maroon stools with fatigue and dyspnea; Hgb 9.8, BUN 28, INR 2.9. Mechanical mitral valve on warfarin; known cecal angiodysplasia; severe aortic stenosis.

Allergies: NKDA.

Course:
- Warfarin held on admission; heparin infusion once INR fell below goal, paused around procedures.
- Hemoglobin stable on serial checks; no transfusion.
- Upper endoscopy 05/20: no bleeding source in the esophagus, stomach or duodenum.
- Colonoscopy 05/20 (same session): no bleeding source; no fresh blood; prior cecal treatment sites healed.
- No further maroon stool after 05/19.
- Warfarin resumed 05/20 evening with heparin overlap; discharged on enoxaparin bridge.

Discharge diagnoses: GI bleeding, source not identified on upper and lower endoscopy; known colonic angiodysplasia. Iron deficiency anemia.
Discharge meds: home medications unchanged (warfarin 5 mg, aspirin 81, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, amlodipine 5, ferrous sulfate 325). Enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h until INR >= 2.5 per PCP.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week (CBC, INR). GI clinic in 6-8 weeks to discuss further small-bowel evaluation.

OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - CLINIC NOTE
Date of service: 07/14/2026

75M with cecal angiodysplasia (APC 01/2025), recurrent bleeding 11/2025 and 05/2026 with no source on CTA, colonoscopy and upper endoscopy; iron deficiency anemia on oral iron; mechanical mitral valve on warfarin; severe aortic stenosis.

Since discharge: no further visible bleeding. Dark stools on iron only. Energy slowly improving.

Meds: warfarin, aspirin 81, lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, ferrous sulfate.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: comfortable. Abdomen benign.

Assessment: Recurrent GI bleeding, source not seen on bidirectional endoscopy after the cecal lesions were treated.

Plan:
1. Small-bowel capsule endoscopy - booked for 09/10/2026. No change to warfarin needed for the capsule; clear liquids the afternoon before and prep per instruction sheet. Hold iron 3 days before.
2. Continue oral iron; CBC per PCP.
3. Return after capsule.

cc: PCP
